$comment: The v2 schema lands in P1 but the apps are adapted in P3 (www) and P5 (admin),
so BUILD §0.2's 'check-types must pass' cannot hold for the apps during P1-P2.
Rather than disable the gate — the failure P0 existed to fix — each package gets
a ceiling. A regression fails the build exactly like a red gate; planned, phased
A ceiling normally only DECREASES. It may rise only when the SCHEMA legitimately
removes more than it did before, which mechanically increases the number of app call
sites that no longer compile. Every such rise is recorded in `history` below with its
cause. A rise with no entry there is the mechanism failing, and should be treated as
one — the whole point of the ratchet is that moving it backwards is conspicuous.

@repo/database.note: green from P1 onward; the schema owner has no excuse

www.note: green from P3 exit; the storefront is fully adapted to v2

admin.note: green from P5 exit; every package is now at zero

@repo/mail.note: new in P2; green from the day it lands

history.why: Initial ceilings, measured immediately after the v2 schema landed. www fell to 138 when apps/www/lib/surface-color.ts was deleted (§22).

Amendment A21. BUILD §3 drops ProductConfiguration.priceIncrease / shippingPrice / discount and renames the model; the first pass dropped only the key/description/isPublic/lampPriceIncrease group and kept the name. Correcting toward the spec removes three more columns and renames a table, so more app call sites stop compiling. Confirmed to be exactly that: every new error is a reference to one of the three dropped columns, to Configuration.productIp, or to an OrderStatus value pruned in 0010. All are P3/P5 adaptation work, none is a regression in code this phase wrote.

The §2.2 search rewrite. apps/www/actions/search.ts now filters through ProductSpec instead of the eight dropped Product columns, reads images from ProductImage, and serialises price as a string. 29 errors cleared.

P2. Removing Clerk changed the shape of ~30 call sites, and the two apps now read user identity from their own database rather than from a provider — which surfaces v1-column references those files already had (product.inventory, product.images, OrderItem.selectedColor, ProductConfiguration.discount). Verified file-by-file: every error is a v2-adaptation site owned by P3 or P5, and NO file P2 authored or rewrote has any error.

P3 storefront adaptation. Service layer rewritten against v2 (translation slugs, ProductImage, ProductSpec, ProductFamily, the stock ledger), the category route tree restructured onto per-locale slugs, every price routed through the money boundary, and every `as unknown as` cast on a Prisma result removed in favour of a derived payload type. www reaches its §26 P3 exit criterion.

P3's shared work cleared 11 admin errors as a side effect - chiefly folding apps/admin/lib/price.ts into @repo/database/money (BUILD 4), which alone accounts for 12 of them (restoring the old formatter measures 111). A ceiling of 98 was briefly set from a mid-phase measurement taken before the last shared edits and never held; 99 is the settled figure. P5 still owns the rest.

P3b. Replacing the admin's third inventory-mutation path with the shared state machine, and routing its low-stock reads through countLowStock, cleared two more. Caught by the budget script, which fails when a package drops below its ceiling.

P5. The admin app is fully adapted to v2: ProductConfiguration, per-locale slugs, ProductImage, the stock ledger, the pruned OrderStatus, and every money value through the Decimal boundary. Every package is now at zero and `check-types` and `check-types:full` are equivalent, which is what BUILD §0.2 asked for from the start.
